headline: Nature paper reports AutoDNA coordinating an AI-native biomolecular laboratory
summary: A Nature paper published on 2026-11-04 introduces AutoDNA, an AI-native biomolecular laboratory. The authors report coordinating more than 20 instrument types over more than 11,000 steps and describe four selected applications, including DNA synthesis, DNA data storage and a KRAS mutation test. They report 3.2-fold faster concurrent protocol execution and exact recovery of stored digital content. These are author-reported results; the full article was not accessible in this review, and the public repository states that full reproduction is not guaranteed without laboratory hardware. No independent reproduction or operational-economics result is established.
